title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (troisième mouture)' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier is a set M of 'figures' carrying three relations: ≤ (subfigure), ≪ (refinement/subdivision) and a relation written ≭ (crossed asymp, roughly 'disposition' or 'non-interference' between figures). Page 23 listed the axioms: the grammar axioms At1–At7, the compatibility/disposition axioms AtC, AtD, AtD0, AtC(spac), AtC(pol), and the 'lieux' axioms AtL1 (divisibility), AtL2, AtL3, AtCL(spac), AtCL(pol).

On this page he states a representation problem: describe the spatial polyhedral ateliers satisfying L1, L2, L3 and AtCL(spac) (or AtCL(pol)) purely in terms of combinatorial data.

Key observation: AtCL lets one recover ≭ on all of M from its restriction to the 'lieux'. The lieux are 𝓛 = {x ∈ M : x minimal for ≪}, the 'points'. On 𝓛 that restriction is a symmetric irreflexive relation ∥, i.e. a graph structure on 𝓛. In the Euclidean atelier x∥y ⇔ x≠y, so there the graph is complete.

The problem is then posed as follows:
- Data: (1) a triple (M, ≤, ≪), (2) the lieux 𝓛 it determines, and (3) a symmetric irreflexive relation ∥ on 𝓛.
- Definition of ≭: for X, Y let L = X∩Y = Sup of the common subfigures Z (Z ≤ X, Z ≤ Y). Set omb(L) := ∪_{Z ≤ X, Y} omb(Z), where omb(X) = {x ∈ 𝓛 : x ≪ X} is the 'shadow' of X (defined explicitly on the next page). Then X ≭ Y iff every x ∈ omb(X)∖omb(L) and every y ∈ omb(Y)∖omb(L) satisfy x∥y. In words: away from their common part, the point-shadows of X and Y are pairwise 'apart'.
- Question: which conditions on (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) make this data come from a genuine special atelier satisfying L1–L3 and AtCL?

The first 'preliminary condition' he writes down is hereditarity (4): X≭Y, X'≤X, Y'≤Y ⇒ X'≭Y'.

The next page carries out the program. It first isolates conditions on ≤ and ≪ alone (ML0, ML1, the latter an Inf-type property for intersections of subfigures with respect to points). It then introduces omb(X), its interior omb(X)°, and proves Lemma 1: X≤Y ⇔ X≪Y ⇔ omb X ⊂ omb Y ⇔ omb(X)° meets omb(Y). So the order structure is recovered from point-shadows.

In modern terms this is a reconstruction theorem for a combinatorial model of tame (polyhedral/stratified) topology. A whole structure of figures, subfigures, subdivisions and relative position is encoded by the poset of figures, its set of points, and a graph on the points.
errors: Condition (4) does not follow formally from definition (3). Write L' = X'∩Y' ≤ L. Then omb(L') ⊂ omb(L), so omb(X')∖omb(L') can contain points of omb(L)∖omb(L') that were never tested in X≭Y. Hereditarity therefore needs an extra hypothesis, essentially that omb(X')∩omb(Y') ⊂ omb(X'∩Y') together with an ML1-type intersection axiom. This is consistent with his own wording that (4) must be 'written' (imposed or derived) rather than merely verified; he corrected 'vérifier' to 'écrire'.

The definition presupposes that Sup_{Z ≤ X, Y} Z exists. At1 only gives sups of filtering bounded families, so existence of this sup (a 'figure intersection') is an unstated assumption. Page 25 addresses it via ML1 and Inf properties.
The letter L is overloaded: script 𝓛 is the set of lieux, while L also denotes the figure X∩Y.

ideas.what: Recovering the disposition/position relation ≭ on all figures from a symmetric irreflexive relation (a graph) on the minimal elements (points), via shadows omb(X)
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of a stratified/polyhedral structure from its point set with an apartness-like graph; face-poset/combinatorial models of tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart; loosely related to face-poset reconstruction (combinatorial topology) and to o-minimal/tame topology (van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: The tame topology program is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6; ateliers are not published

ideas.what: Representation problem: characterize the data (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) that arise from special polyhedral ateliers satisfying L1–L3 and AtCL
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic/combinatorial characterization of polyhedral or stratified spaces

ideas.what: Hereditarity of the disposition relation under passing to subfigures (condition 4)
ideas.modern_name: Monotonicity/hereditary property of a binary relation

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a representation theorem for polyhedral 'ateliers': the whole relative-position structure should be determined by the subfigure/refinement poset together with a graph on the points. Only preliminary conditions and a first lemma are worked out here and on the next page. No published axiomatization of tame topology of this form is known to me.
missed.quote: la condition AtCL(spec) nous réduit, pour connaître ≭_M, à la connaissance de ∦_L, i.e. à celle d'une structure de graphes sur L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a purely order-theoretic and graph-theoretic axiomatization of tame/polyhedral topology. This is relevant to synthetic or combinatorial approaches to o-minimal geometry and to finite models of stratified spaces.

missed.claim: The relation ∥ on points is symmetric and irreflexive and coincides with ≠ in the Euclidean case. That is formally the shape of an apartness relation from constructive mathematics; non-Euclidean ateliers would then carry coarser apartness. The link is not made explicit by Grothendieck and is speculative.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could connect Grothendieck's tame topology program with constructive/point-free topology (apartness spaces, locales). This is speculative.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished piece of Grothendieck's axiomatic tame-topology ('ateliers') program and contains a clear reconstruction idea (position relations from a graph on points). The mathematics on the page itself is mostly problem-setting and definitions, with no completed result.
transcription_corrections: 'comb(X)', 'comb(Y)', 'comb(L)', 'comb(Z)' should read 'omb(X)', 'omb(Y)', 'omb(L)', 'omb(Z)': '∀x ∈ omb(X)∖omb(L)'. This is the shadow notation defined on p.25.
'AB dans le cas d'un atelier euclidien' should be 'NB dans le cas d'un atelier euclidien'.
'ateliers spéciaux polyédraux' and 'AtCL(spéc/spec)' are likely 'spaciaux' / 'AtCL(spac)', consistent with the notation on p.23.
'rel. bin. symétriques antiréflexives' is more likely 'relations symétriques antiréflexives'. An interlinear insertion above it seems to give 'symétriques' / 'de graphes'.
The set of lieux is written as a script 𝓛, distinct from the figure L = X∩Y.
